policy.adoptionRule: No component may be marked adopted without verified license, official source, defined capability gap, test evidence, security review, cost review, rollback path, and owner.
policy.paidRule: Free/open/local/free-credit routes are preferred. Any paid dependency requires explicit founder approval before becoming operational infrastructure.
policy.architectureRule: Prefer adapters and replaceable capability interfaces over hard coupling to a provider or model.

components.name: HyperFrames
components.capabilityGap: Agent-friendly deterministic composition, motion graphics, captions, HTML-native video rendering and repeatable MP4 output without per-render fees.
components.whyCandidate: Strong fit for the Studio OS assembly/render layer; active releases; explicit agent skills; deterministic output; commercial-friendly license.
risks: Requires Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg
Generated-source media still depends on upstream providers
Must keep Studio OS abstractions independent from HyperFrames-specific formats
components.costPosition: Core rendering is open-source with no per-render fee; compute remains local/self-hosted unless optional cloud rendering is used.
components.test: Build one 10-15 second We Were Something proof sequence from existing assets with audio, title/caption layer, deterministic rerender and frame snapshots.
acceptance: Same inputs reproduce equivalent frames
MP4 renders locally
No paid API required for assembly
Receipt/evidence includes source assets, command and output hash
Can be invoked behind a Studio OS adapter

components.name: Kinocut
components.capabilityGap: Guardrailed FFmpeg editing, typed agent tools, quality gates and Video Receipts for evidence-backed completion.
components.whyCandidate: Directly addresses the historic gap between generated assets and verifiable edited deliverables; local-first and designed for MCP/agent use.
risks: Younger/smaller project than mature editors
Requires FFmpeg
Need to verify receipt and QC semantics against CA creative gates rather than accepting defaults
components.costPosition: Free/open-source local processing; no credit-metered SaaS required for core editing.
components.test: Run the same We Were Something proof assets through trim/assemble/audio-normalize/QC and produce a Video Receipt; compare output and ergonomics with HyperFrames.
acceptance: Produces inspectable receipt
Quality gate can fail a deliberately broken input
No paid API required for core edit
Can be rerun deterministically enough for audit
Can coexist with HyperFrames rather than duplicate it

components.name: OpenMontage
components.capabilityGap: Pipeline manifests, stage director skills, checkpoints, self-review, provider routing and human approval gates for agentic video production.
components.whyCandidate: Very strong architectural reference for the production-control plane and directly overlaps Studio OS orchestration requirements.
risks: AGPL-3.0 creates material copyleft obligations if code is incorporated into a networked commercial product
Large and fast-moving surface area
High issue/PR volume suggests integration churn
Potential provider/API costs
components.costPosition: Software is open source; configured providers may be paid. Do not make it a paid dependency by default.
components.test: Architecture/black-box benchmark first. Do not copy AGPL code into proprietary Studio OS until licensing strategy is explicitly approved.
acceptance: Extract useful interface patterns without license contamination
Demonstrate checkpoint/recovery on a disposable test project
Identify which controls Studio OS already has and which are missing
No production adoption without legal/license decision

components.name: MoneyPrinterTurbo
components.capabilityGap: Automated topic-to-script-to-assets-to-voice-to-captions-to-render pipeline for low-cost social/explainer content.
components.whyCandidate: Useful specialist workflow and architectural reference; permissive license; relevant to CA social/RS demonstrations rather than flagship cinematic generation.
risks: Default workflow is closer to stock-footage automation than premium cinema
External LLM/media/TTS providers can introduce cost or rights constraints
Public deployment/security must be reviewed
components.costPosition: Core software is MIT; zero-cost operation depends on selected providers and source media.
components.test: Create one CA/RS explainer/social proof using only free/local-compatible services and record every dependency/cost/right.
acceptance: No unapproved paid call
All source-media rights recorded
Output is editable after generation
Workflow can be called as a specialist Studio OS capability

components.name: OpenVid
components.capabilityGap: Polished screen/demo video treatment, camera movement, framing and presentation without consuming generative-video credits.
components.whyCandidate: Potentially valuable for RS/Studio OS product demos and presentation polish; not a replacement for generative footage.
risks: License must be reverified from canonical repository before adoption
Narrow specialist scope
Browser rendering constraints require benchmark
components.costPosition: Expected local/browser processing; confirm all dependencies before test.
components.test: Verify canonical license and current release, then polish a 10-second Studio OS screen recording and measure render/export quality.
acceptance: License verified
4K/target export works on supported environment
No paid API required for core treatment

components.name: JoyAI-Video-Edit
components.capabilityGap: Instruction-led transformation/repair of existing generated video while preserving temporal continuity.
components.whyCandidate: Could reduce expensive full-shot regeneration when only environment/style/subject details need correction.
risks: Very high compute requirements
Practical zero-cost hosted route not established
Dependency/runtime maturity must be validated
License and model-weight terms must be checked separately
components.costPosition: Not considered a practical zero-cost operational route until suitable hosted/free compute is proven.
components.test: Reopen when a verified free compute route or consumer-GPU path exists; use one failed CA shot as repair benchmark.
acceptance: Commercial/model terms verified
Compute cost within approved budget
Identity/temporal consistency measurably improves vs regeneration

components.name: Donkey Cut
components.capabilityGap: Human-friendly timeline/editor surface with conversational assistance for assembling generated footage.
components.whyCandidate: Could become a review/edit surface while Studio OS remains the intelligence/control layer.
risks: Canonical repository, license and current free-vs-credit boundaries must be reverified
AI generation features may incur third-party costs
Potential overlap with Kinocut/HyperFrames
components.costPosition: Core editor may be free/open; paid generation must never be assumed free.
components.test: Verify canonical repo/license, then compare the same proof edit against Kinocut for human review ergonomics and export.
acceptance: License verified
Core editing usable without paid credits
Project remains editable/exportable
Distinct value over Kinocut is demonstrated

components.name: TencentDB Agent Memory
components.capabilityGap: Long-term agent memory and progressive compression for persistent project context.
components.whyCandidate: Potential relevance to Studio OS continuity, but must not replace the canonical GitHub/D1 organisational record without strong evidence.
risks: Canonical source and license not yet verified in this pass
Memory frameworks can create hidden state and provenance problems
May duplicate existing D1 knowledge/decision/asset model
components.costPosition: Unknown until canonical project and hosting requirements are verified.
components.test: Verify official repository/license first; benchmark retrieval accuracy, provenance, deletion/update semantics and recovery against existing D1 records.
acceptance: Canonical source verified
No silent overwrite of canon
Every recalled fact has provenance
Improves retrieval without becoming source of truth
